key_insight: Bellman updates in continuous-state/action Q-learning gain anisotropic regularity under Hölder-regular diffusion dynamics, smoothing in state while remaining only Lipschitz in action.
engineering_relevance: The result motivates tensor-product DeepONet-style approximators and provides explicit complexity bounds for designing scalable value-function surrogates in continuous stochastic control.
method: Analyze the Bellman optimality target in a diffusion control setting.
Prove the Bellman operator maps bounded inputs into an anisotropic Hölder/Lipschitz class.
Derive approximation and resource bounds plus a stiffness–complexity trade-off as the time step δ→0.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical regularity, compactness, and approximation/resource bounds rather than empirical experiments or benchmark data.
watch_item: The theory does not establish full convergence for practical sampled Q-learning with exploration, replay buffers, or stochastic gradient-based training.
